editorial: When a midnight scream pierces the fog, you’re drawn into a dark, cerebral corridor of revenge. In Oddity, the psychological thriller becomes an elaborate scavenger hunt, with each haunted relic holding a clue that turns emotion into weapon. The cinematography, led by an art-deco set that feels both haunted and hyperreal, turns each flashback into an unsettling dance of shadows. However, the pacing falters halfway through, as the thriller stumbles into a repetitive loop of clunky encounters. Ideal for fans of psychological thrillers who enjoy non-linear storytelling.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of psychological thrillers who enjoy non-linear storytelling.
